tasks.short: Keep pension fund, insurer and broker records in line with AFAS, and sort out mismatches and employee questions.

today.trigger: Monthly payroll close, a new hire, a leaver, a contract change, or a carrier or broker invoice or mutation list arriving.
steps: Export joiners, leavers and salary changes from AFAS Profit to Excel
Compare with the Pensioenfonds Vervoer and insurer portal records and the broker's premium invoice
Chase differences by mail with the Payroll Specialist, the broker or the fund
Correct records in AFAS or the carrier portal and file the proof on SharePoint
Answer employee pension and insurance questions by mail and Teams
drudgery: Matching employee numbers and premium lines row by row in Excel
Retyping the same mutation into AFAS and a carrier portal
today.time_sinks: Monthly reconciliation of premium invoices against AFAS and chasing small differences that turn out to be timing, plus repeated questions about the new pension scheme.

lenses.faster: A scheduled reconciliation matches AFAS mutations against carrier files and invoices and lists only real differences, so the Excel matching disappears and the specialist spends about an hour a month on exceptions instead of a day.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract and each carrier file trigger the match; clean records pass on their own, and the specialist approves each correction before it goes to the fund or broker.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to employees: a pension and insurance question desk that answers from fund documents in Dutch, Polish and English for shift workers who never reach HR in office hours; demand would grow as it got cheaper, especially around the 2027 scheme change.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the row-by-row premium matching; the specialist wants more time explaining the new pension scheme to people it affects.
lenses.options: Little here: reconciliation has one right answer, so drafts do not change the decision.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from checking lines to owning the carrier contracts and data agreements, deciding when a recurring mismatch means renegotiating with the broker; somewhat more expert.
reach: Payroll Specialist: absorb the monthly pension premium deduction check, after learning the AFAS payroll components
HR Administrator: take over benefits mutations at entry and exit, which needs no new skill

tasks.human_edge: Judging a case that the rules do not cover, such as a long-term sick driver's pension accrual during the scheme transition, and explaining a loss or choice to a worried employee in plain words.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching AFAS records to carrier files and invoices follows fixed rules and keys, so code built quickly with AI can run it without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract and each carrier file or broker invoice landing in a SharePoint folder.
steps: Load AFAS joiners, leavers and pensionable salary changes
Match against fund, insurer and broker files on employee number and period
Post clean matches and list differences with likely cause
Draft correction notes for the fund or broker
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every correction and every message to a carrier before it is sent.
systems: Excel or Power BI exception view
data_needed: AFAS employee, contract and salary mutations
Carrier mutation files and premium invoices
in_practice.logs_to: An exception log on SharePoint with each match result, correction and approver.

evidence.claim: Pensioenfonds Vervoer expects its new scheme on 1 January 2027, which will drive extra mutations and questions.
That Noordhaven's drivers fall under Pensioenfonds Vervoer is assumed, not confirmed.
Rule-based reconciliation of HR records to carrier files is routine software work.

risks: Carrier file formats change without notice and break the match
Pension data is personal data under AVG; the tool needs a clear processing basis and access limits
A question desk on pensions must say it is AI (AI Act Art. 50) and must not give advice that only the fund may give
research_questions: Which carriers and brokers deliver machine-readable mutation files, and in what format?
How many hours a month go to reconciliation today, measured over three closes?
What share of differences are timing versus real errors?
Which employee groups sit in which pension scheme after 1 January 2027?

tasks.short: Grade a new or changed job, decide CAO scale or own scale, and set its salary range.

today.trigger: A manager asks for a new role, a reorganisation changes a role, or Recruitee needs a range before a vacancy opens.
steps: Collect the job description and talk to the manager
Score the job against the grading system or the CAO function list
Compare with similar roles in AFAS and on other sites
Set scale, overtime eligibility and range, and write the grading memo
Record the outcome in AFAS and tell the manager
drudgery: Rewriting vague manager descriptions into the factor format
Searching old grading memos for comparable roles
today.time_sinks: Getting a usable job description out of a busy manager and writing up the reasoning per factor.

lenses.faster: A model turns the manager's notes into a structured description and a draft grade per factor with reasons and comparable roles, so the specialist checks and decides in about an hour instead of half a day.
lenses.autonomous: A grading request in Recruitee or a form starts the draft; nothing counts until the specialist sets the grade.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: re-check grades of changed roles at every reorganisation and yearly, not only when someone complains, which pay transparency will demand; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rewriting manager notes; the specialist wants more time on the hard borderline calls and talking to the people who do the job.
lenses.options: Two or three draft gradings with different readings of responsibility make the borderline choice visible before the manager pushes for the higher scale.
lenses.altitude: The specialist stops writing memos and owns consistency across the whole job grid, with the right to refuse grades that break it; more expert.
reach: Recruiter: set the pay range shown in vacancies, which pay transparency requires before negotiation
HR Business Partner: run the first intake with managers using the same structured form

tasks.human_edge: Seeing what a job really demands on the warehouse floor, weighing the manager's interest in a higher grade, and standing behind the grade with the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns messy notes into a checkable description and per-factor draft inside a fixed grading workflow; the grade itself stays a human decision.

in_practice.trigger: A grading request form submitted by a manager or recruiter.
steps: Model drafts the description on skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions
Model proposes a grade per factor with reasons and the three closest existing roles
Specialist sets grade, scale and range
Approved grade is written to AFAS job scheme fields
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist decides every grade; CAO jobs stay inside the CAO function system.
data_needed: Grading system and CAO function lists
in_practice.logs_to: Grading file per job on SharePoint with draft, final grade, reasons and decider, linked to the AFAS job scheme.

evidence.claim: A UK university graded 50 job descriptions with ChatGPT per HERA factor at over 70% agreement with experts.
The Dutch pay transparency bill requires job evaluation on skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions, with works council consent.
Practitioners advise against regrading when core accountabilities have not materially changed.
AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as preparation for pay transparency.

risks: About 30% of draft grades may be wrong, and a wrong grade becomes an unexplained pay difference
Grade recommendations may fall under AI Act Annex III high-risk from December 2027, with logging and works council information duties
Anchoring: the specialist may accept the draft too easily
research_questions: How often does the draft grade match the specialist's final grade over 30 recent cases?
Does the works council accept a model draft inside the grading procedure?
Which roles fall outside the CAO function lists and need the own system?

tasks.short: Look into what other employers and the law do on benefits and safety, and propose changes to our policies.

today.trigger: A new law or CAO change, a retention or absence trend, or a question from the HR Director or works council.
steps: Search law sites, CAO texts, benchmark reports and peer contacts
Compare with Noordhaven's policies on SharePoint
Estimate cost with AFAS and Power BI figures
Write a recommendation memo or slides for the HR Director
drudgery: Reading long legal and CAO texts for the one changed clause
Building the policy comparison table by hand
today.time_sinks: Reading and summarising sources, and comparing them clause by clause with current policy.

lenses.faster: A research assistant collects sources, compares them with current SharePoint policies and drafts the memo with citations, so the specialist spends their time checking sources and costing.
lenses.autonomous: A watch on law, CAO and fund publications flags changes weekly with a short impact note; the specialist decides what goes further.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: benefits and safety proposals built for flex workers and night shifts, who count in the pay gap report and drive 90-day retention; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses reading 80 pages for one clause; the specialist wants more time testing ideas with employees and the works council.
lenses.options: Two or three policy variants with costs and who they help let the HR Director choose rather than approve one proposal.
lenses.altitude: The specialist becomes the person who tells the HR Director which benefit changes pay off in retention and absence; more expert.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: link benefit uptake to retention and verzuim in Power BI, after learning basic DAX
HR Business Partner: brief site managers on policy changes

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what works on the floor in Rotterdam versus Venlo, what the works council will accept, and which source is trustworthy.
tasks.pattern_why: The question and sources vary each time, and the person leads the judgment on what to recommend.

in_practice.trigger: A research question from the HR Director or a flagged change in law, CAO or fund rules.
steps: Assistant gathers and summarises sources with links
Assistant compares them with current SharePoint policies
Specialist checks sources and adds costing from AFAS
Specialist finalises the recommendation
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist checks every cited source and signs the recommendation.
data_needed: Benefit uptake and cost from AFAS
Absence and retention from Power BI
in_practice.logs_to: Recommendation memo with source list on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: 49% of 500 employers say salary structures lag and 61% are rewriting job descriptions for AI.
Pensioenfonds Vervoer's new scheme from 1 January 2027 is a live policy topic.
General-purpose assistants can summarise and compare policy texts with citations.

risks: Invented or outdated legal citations
US-centric sources that do not fit Dutch law
Recommendations that need works council consent being presented as decided
research_questions: How many research memos a year, and how long each takes today?
Do drafted comparisons catch the changed clauses a specialist would catch?
Which benefit changes in the last two years moved retention or absence?

tasks.short: Answer manager and employee questions on the CAO, pay and benefit rules, and HR procedures.

today.trigger: A mail, Teams message or call from a manager or employee.
steps: Read the question and check the person's contract and scale in AFAS
Look up the CAO article, policy or law
Write the answer, sometimes after checking with a colleague
Keep the mail for reference
drudgery: Answering the same shift allowance and leave questions every week
Looking up the same CAO articles again
today.time_sinks: Repeat questions and finding the right clause across two CAOs and local policies.

lenses.faster: A drafted answer with the cited CAO article and policy arrives with each question, so the specialist checks and sends in minutes; routine questions take a fraction of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A question in a shared mailbox or Teams starts a draft; the specialist approves each reply, and pay transparency requests are tracked against the two-month deadline.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to employees: individual pay information requests under the pay transparency law answered with their band and group averages; demand will rise once the law starts.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the tenth shift allowance answer this month; the specialist wants more time coaching managers on hard cases.
lenses.options: Little here: most questions have one correct answer.
lenses.altitude: The specialist reviews answers instead of writing them and owns the question bank that shows where policies confuse people; about as expert.
reach: HR Administrator: first-line pay and benefit questions handled with the same approved answer bank
HR Business Partner: the CAO side of manager advice

tasks.human_edge: Hearing the real problem behind a question, knowing when a question is the start of a complaint, and handling sensitive personal situations.
tasks.pattern_why: Each question needs different lookups in AFAS, CAOs and policies that cannot be fixed in advance; the specialist approves before anything is sent.

in_practice.trigger: A question in the HR pay and benefits mailbox or Teams channel.
steps: Agent classifies the question and pulls contract and scale from AFAS
Agent finds the CAO article or policy and drafts the answer with citations
Specialist edits and approves
Reply is sent and added to the answer bank
in_practice.human_gate: Every reply is approved by the specialist; complaints and individual pay requests are routed to the specialist without a draft send.
in_practice.logs_to: Question log with draft, final reply, sources and approver; pay requests with date received and answered.

evidence.claim: Pay transparency requires answering individual pay requests within two months.
A chatbot answering employees must disclose that it is AI (AI Act Art. 50).
Retrieval over policy documents with cited answers is common practice.

risks: A wrong CAO interpretation sent under the specialist's name
Personal pay data exposed to the wrong person
Approval becomes a rubber stamp at volume
research_questions: How many questions a week, and what share repeats?
How often does the draft cite the right article in a test of 50 past questions?
Which questions must never get a draft, per the works council?

tasks.short: Run the yearly merit round and bonus schemes, from budget and rules to manager input and payroll.

today.trigger: The yearly budget cycle and merit round, or a new incentive scheme for a site or role.
steps: Build merit budget and guidelines in Excel from AFAS salaries
Send manager sheets and collect proposals
Check proposals against budget, scale and rules, and chase outliers
Get approval and hand changes to the Payroll Specialist
Write letters for employees
drudgery: Checking each proposal against scale maximums by hand
today.time_sinks: Spreadsheet merging and chasing managers for corrections.

lenses.faster: Budget rules and checks run as software on AFAS data and an assistant drafts scheme texts and letters, so merging and checking drop and the specialist spends time on outliers.
lenses.autonomous: Manager proposals are checked against budget, scale and gap rules on entry; the specialist and HR Director approve, and no pay change is made by the model alone.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made more often: test each proposal for its effect on the gender and group pay gap before approval rather than once a year afterwards; demand will grow with pay transparency.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses merging spreadsheets; the specialist wants more time designing schemes that keep people past 90 days.
lenses.options: Several budget scenarios showing cost, gap effect and retention risk change which split between sites and groups the HR Director picks.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the merit and incentive design and the evidence that every pay difference is explainable; more expert.
reach: FP&A Analyst: personnel cost forecast for the merit round, after learning the budget model
Payroll Specialist: preparing AFAS import of approved changes

tasks.human_edge: Judging fairness between people and sites, handling manager pressure, and deciding what the company will and will not reward.
tasks.pattern_why: Scheme design and approval are judgment calls led by the person; the AI drafts scenarios and checks, it does not decide pay.

in_practice.trigger: Start of the merit round or a request for a new incentive scheme.
steps: Assistant builds budget scenarios from AFAS data
Rule checks flag proposals above scale, budget or gap thresholds
Specialist reviews flags with managers
Approved changes go to payroll and letters are drafted
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist and HR Director approve every pay change; no change is decided solely by a model (GDPR Art. 22).
in_practice.logs_to: Merit file per round with proposals, flags, decisions and approvers.

evidence.claim: Pay recommendations can fall under AI Act Annex III 4(b), high-risk from 2 December 2027.
Paying for AI-driven gains is unsettled; Zapier's pilot has not run and credit is case-by-case.
GDPR Art. 22 bars a pay decision made solely by a model.

risks: Bias in performance data carried into merit proposals
Works council consent needed for scheme changes under WOR 27
Over-reliance on scenario outputs
research_questions: How many hours does the merit round take today, split by step?
Is there a merit round outside the CAO scales at all, and for how many people?
Does the works council see a scenario tool as part of the pay system?

tasks.short: Advise on complaints from staff who think their grade or pay is wrong.

today.trigger: An employee or their manager objects to a grade or salary, formally or informally.
steps: Collect the grading file, contract and pay history from AFAS
Talk to the employee and manager
Compare with similar roles and the CAO
Write advice for the HR Director or complaints committee
drudgery: Assembling the file from scattered mails and old memos
Building the peer comparison by hand
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the history of the grade and finding comparable roles.

lenses.faster: An assistant assembles the case file, timeline and peer comparison, so the specialist starts from a complete file and spends time on the conversation and the advice.
lenses.autonomous: Not suited: a complaint opens a case file automatically, but every step after that stays with the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made more often: check pay differences proactively within the six-month window before they become complaints or a joint evaluation with the works council.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses digging through old mails; the specialist wants more time listening to the employee.
lenses.options: Laying out two readings of the grade with their consequences for peers helps the committee decide.
lenses.altitude: The specialist handles fewer surprise complaints and more early fixes; equally expert, more trusted.
reach: HR Business Partner: first conversation with the employee, using the prepared file

tasks.human_edge: Trust, listening, and judging fairness in a contested case where the employee's livelihood is at stake.
tasks.pattern_why: Complaints are human-led; AI only prepares files and comparisons.

steps: Assistant assembles grading history, contract and pay data
Assistant builds a peer comparison
Specialist talks to the parties and writes the advice
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist writes and owns the advice; no model text goes to the employee.
in_practice.logs_to: Complaint case file on SharePoint with restricted access.

evidence.claim: An unexplained gap of 5% or more after six months triggers a joint evaluation with the works council.
Works council consent covers the grading system under WOR 27(1)(c).

risks: Sensitive personal data in a model context
Employee distrust if they learn AI was involved
Comparison groups chosen wrongly
research_questions: How many grade and pay complaints a year, and how long each takes?
How long does file assembly take versus advice writing?
Will employees and the works council accept AI-prepared files?

tasks.short: Write job descriptions, keep the job grid and salary scales up to date.

today.trigger: New roles, reorganisations, CAO scale changes, or preparation for pay transparency.
steps: Draft or update job descriptions in Word from templates on SharePoint
Place jobs in job families and grades
Update salary scales in Excel after CAO raises
Load scales and job schemes into AFAS
drudgery: Re-keying scale tables after each CAO raise
today.time_sinks: Keeping hundreds of descriptions consistent and current.

lenses.faster: Descriptions are drafted in the four-factor format and scale tables recalculated by rules from the CAO raise, so the specialist reviews instead of writes.
lenses.autonomous: A CAO raise or a new role triggers draft descriptions and recalculated scales; the specialist approves before they enter AFAS.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the works council and HR Director: a complete, consistent job architecture across three sites ready for pay transparency reporting over 2027.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses template formatting; the specialist wants more time on the job architecture itself.
lenses.options: Alternative job family groupings show different gap outcomes, which changes the grouping chosen with the works council.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the job architecture and its evidence base; more expert.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: maintaining job scheme fields in AFAS
Recruiter: vacancy texts from the approved description

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what a job is for, grouping jobs fairly, and agreeing the result with the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns notes into a structured description in a fixed workflow; scale tables are plain rules.

in_practice.trigger: New role request, reorganisation or CAO raise.
steps: Model drafts description in the four-factor template
Rules recalculate scales from the CAO raise
Specialist reviews and approves
Approved data loads into AFAS job schemes
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every description and scale before it enters AFAS.
in_practice.logs_to: Versioned job description library on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories for pay transparency.
CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties are regrading the sector's jobs, outcome pending.
Model grading from descriptions reached over 70% agreement with experts in a UK pilot.

risks: Sector regrading may overrule own work
Generic descriptions that miss site-specific demands
Works council consent needed for grouping
research_questions: How many job descriptions exist and how many are outdated?
When will the CAO regrading land?
Which jobs fall outside the CAO?

tasks.short: Cost CAO proposals and pay scenarios for bargaining and budget.

today.trigger: CAO negotiations, a union proposal, or a budget question from the Finance Director.
steps: Extract headcount, scales and hours from AFAS
Build cost model in Excel per proposal
Run scenarios for raises, allowances and flex workers
Present results to HR and Finance Directors
drudgery: Rebuilding the Excel model for each new proposal
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding and checking spreadsheet models during negotiation rounds.

lenses.faster: A tested costing model on the AFAS extract runs each proposal in minutes, and an assistant drafts the summary, so the specialist checks assumptions instead of formulas.
lenses.autonomous: A new proposal entered as parameters runs the costing automatically; the specialist approves results before they go to the table.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made more often: cost every counter-proposal during the negotiation day rather than overnight, including agency flex workers.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding formulas at midnight; the specialist wants more time on negotiation strategy.
lenses.options: Several costed scenarios side by side change which package the company offers.
lenses.altitude: The specialist becomes the cost adviser in the negotiation room; more expert.
reach: FP&A Analyst: personnel cost scenarios in the budget
Controller: provisions for CAO back pay

tasks.human_edge: Choosing assumptions, reading the other side, and judging what is affordable and acceptable.
tasks.pattern_why: Costing is arithmetic on known data and parameters; build once, run without a model.

steps: Enter proposal parameters
Model computes cost per group, site and year from AFAS data
Specialist checks assumptions and results
Summary goes to directors
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves each costing before it is shared.
data_needed: Flex worker volumes and agency rates

evidence.claim: Compa Analyst Agent with Mercer data drafts market-pricing findings; no customer result published.
Sector CAO regrading is under negotiation.

risks: Wrong assumptions presented as precise numbers
Agency data incomplete
Model drift from AFAS field changes
research_questions: How many costing rounds per CAO cycle?
Is agency pay data available in usable form?
Does Finance accept a shared costing model?

role.altitude: From grading jobs and reconciling records one by one to owning Noordhaven's job architecture, pay evidence and benefit design, with the right to block grades and pay changes that cannot be explained under pay transparency.
reach: Payroll Specialist: pension premium and benefit deduction checks
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: pay gap reporting from AFAS
role.ceiling_note: Perhaps 300 to 400 hours a year can move off reconciliation, drafting and file work; complaints, negotiation, works council consent and pay decisions stay human, and AI Act and GDPR Art. 22 limit how far pay recommendations can go.
skills_to_grow: Pay transparency job evaluation and gap analysis
Building and testing rule-based tools on the AFAS extract
AI Act high-risk oversight and logging
role.ambitious_version: Run a pay transparency service for the whole company, including flex workers, that answers every individual pay request within two months and explains every pay difference before the first report over 2027 is due.
